core_meaning.short_meaning: Resilient desert plant; companion Thumamah ibn Uthal, chieftain of Yamama.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Thumamah (ثُمَامَة) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning 'a resilient desert plant' or 'pliant, sweet-natured vitality'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Thumamah ibn Uthal al-Hanafi, chieftain of the Banu Hanifa, whose transformation upon witnessing the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Medina led to one of the most famous conversions in early Islam.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: A stalk or bundle of thumām (a sweet-scented desert grass noted for bendable resilience in dry winds).
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Thumamah was captured as a prisoner of war and tied to a pillar in the Prophet's Mosque in Medina. The Prophet ﷺ treated him with gracious hospitality for three days without coercion. When released unconditionally, Thumamah walked to a nearby palm grove, washed himself, and returned to declare Islam before the Prophet ﷺ. He then went directly to Mecca to perform Umrah, becoming the first Muslim to openly recite the Talbiyah before the Quraysh.
